comments.text:
Hi Dr. Mike, fellow Biochemist & Molecular Biologist here. A really great video on this topic.
I work since my PhD in the field of Proteomics and have been working with Peptides all the time. I just got off guard with this topic and did not know that it suddenly gets so much attention. In the end as you said corrently, Proteins are made of chains of amino acids and there are currently different fields exploring the world of tiny proteins or even peptides (Peptidomics) especially in the context of immunology and then of course peptides are in my world just the break down of proteins with an enzyme (e.g. trypsin) which then I measure on my mass spectrometer (analyzes mass to charge ratio). 
Peptides can have a function but this is still being researched on and some researcher say it does influence others say the cells might not really respond to it or might additional factors to translate it into a measurable signal. 
I totally agree that we need to have more evidence and research on if small peptides really have an influence on certain diseases. I cannot believe that people really inject unregulated substances. I could provide a peptide mixture from my cell culture cells and sell that without having to show if it really works. I just cannot believe where we got with our longevity hype. What really blew my mind was the vote against the FDA scientist. This is clearly showing that we have moved away from evidence based rational to just gut feeling. Not sure what to say anymore just one thing: Dear all, please don't just buy what wellness influencer or any other scientific sounding "expert" wants you to inject or swallow. Keep in mind to fact check and talk to your doctor and a scientist if you have one in your family. We are all here to help you and put things in perspective and context. Thanks for making this video Dr. Mike! Keep up your awesome work!
comments.author: @DDHS_Podcast
